---
title: "05 · Covariance shape"
description: "Why diffuse shape information pays a quadratic compression price."
---

Local Gaussian perturbations decompose into mean, overall log scale, and
traceless covariance shape. Haar averaging retains `m/d` of mean and scale
information, but only

$$\frac{(m-1)(m+2)}{(d-1)(d+2)}\sim(m/d)^2$$

of a diffuse, scale-adjusted shape direction.

```python
from rpgeom.ceilings import mean_ratio, shape_ratio
print(mean_ratio(8, 40), shape_ratio(8, 40))
```

Finite-rank spikes are not diffuse. Their detectability also depends on sample
size and spike strength; do not apply the quadratic rate to them without a model.
